description_full: Plumas Bancorp operates as the bank holding company for the Plumas Bank that provides various banking products and services for small and middle market businesses and individuals. The company accepts various deposits, such as checking, money market checking, business sweep, public funds sweep, savings, and retirement accounts, as well as time and remote deposits. Its loan portfolio comprises personal and commercial loans, real estate, construction, agricultural, and government-guaranteed loans; residential and home equity lines of credit; land development and construction loans; automobile loans; consumer loans; purchased credit deteriorated (PCD) and non-PCD loans; and small business administration loans. In addition, the company provides telephone and mobile banking, internet banking with bill-pay options, cashier's check, bank-by-mail, automated teller machine, night depository, safe deposit box, direct and mobile deposit, electronic funds transfer, FedNow®-receive Service, and other customary banking services. Plumas Bancorp was founded in 1980 and is headquartered in Reno, Nevada.

financial_summary: Plumas Bancorp is a small-cap financial services business with a $430M market cap on $98M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +13% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +2.5pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 48% against a 7% cost of capital — a 41-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $20M in free cash flow — roughly 21 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, with adequate 0.73× cash conversion.

On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and thin 2.8× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Shareholder yield is only 1.8%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 6.4% of the shares, and within its sector the business captures 1.5× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
